requirement_text: Internally to the CPN a CNG receiving private or other critical information (i.e. from a CND) should verify that the data was protected from unauthorised disclosure.
rationale: Protection from unauthorized disclosure is a confidentiality concern. The statement also prescribes a verification action, so the NFR label is plausible rather than independently established.

requirement_text: The CNG should detect replayed user and/or device credentials.
rationale: Detecting replayed credentials is an observable security function. NFR is plausible under a security-topic convention, while a behaviour-based definition also supports a functional reading.

requirement_text: When the CNG detects replayed user and/or device credentials the CNG shall stop the relevant processes.
rationale: The condition and response specify stopping processes after credential replay. FR describes that behaviour; the supplied NFR label reflects its security purpose. The disagreement alone does not establish a model mistake.

requirement_text: On detection of a message integrity error at the CNG the CNG shall discard the message.
rationale: Discarding a message after an integrity error is specified system behaviour serving a security constraint. Both aspects occur in the same statement.

requirement_text: On receipt of a valid (i.e. authorized) request for data stored in the CNG the CNG shall return the requested data to the requesting user.
rationale: Returning requested stored data after a valid request describes an input-response function. Authorization is a precondition, with no separate quality target. FR is defensible under the report's behaviour definition; the published NFR label is retained.

requirement_text: The CNG shall support mechanisms to authenticate itself to the NGN for service usage purposes.
rationale: Supporting authentication mechanisms specifies a security capability. Compare FR-labelled row 3276, which also requires support for an authentication protocol. This is a label-convention concern, not a basis for automatically changing either label.

requirement_text: CPN environment shall be protected with a stateful firewall function that may be implemented in the CNG.
rationale: A stateful firewall is a security mechanism and an architectural choice. The NFR label is plausible as a security/design constraint, while the mechanism also provides functions.

requirement_text: The CNG and the CPN shall be able to support parental control related functionalities limiting the use of the broadband connection on a user or time basis. Limitations on a content basis may be shared with devoted network servers.
rationale: Parental-control functions enforce user-, time- and content-based restrictions. This combines named functions with access restrictions, making an exclusive FR/NFR interpretation dependent on the annotation convention.

requirement_text: The CNG should negotiate session parameters (bandwidth screen resolution codecs…) with the NGN transparently to the user.
rationale: Negotiating session parameters is an observable network function. The phrase transparently to the user adds a quality aspect, but the main action supports the FR label.

requirement_text: Standard NGN authentication routing and connectivity should be used to establish remote access connectivity.
rationale: The statement both supports remote access and prescribes standard authentication/routing mechanisms. This may be read as a function or an implementation/security constraint; the NFR prediction is not automatically a clear semantic error.

requirement_text: The CNG should be able to assist in establishing Rich Communication Suite sessions between CNDs including joining/splitting voice & media streams.
rationale: Establishing communication sessions and joining or splitting media streams are system capabilities. No measurable quality target is stated. The NFR prediction conflicts with a plausible functional reference.

requirement_text: The CNG shall support intra-CPN communication between IMS and non-IMS capable CNDs.
rationale: Supporting communication between two types of network devices specifies a capability. The terminology is specialized, but no quality-level constraint is stated.

requirement_text: The CNG shall support the connection to a STB (or media gateway) both in a bridged or in a routed mode of operation.
rationale: Supporting bridged and routed connections to another device specifies supported operating modes and connectivity behaviour. The FR reference is plausible.

requirement_text: In case of managed services QoS rules applied by CNG shall be configurable by a remote management system.
rationale: Remote configurability is a function, while the configured objects are quality-of-service rules. The statement combines a management capability with a quality-related subject.

requirement_text: A suitably authorized CPN user (e.g. the system administrator) shall be able to install and activate NGN managed services without the intervention of the subscribing CPN user.
rationale: An authorized administrator installing and activating services is a concrete role-based operation. Authorization alone does not remove its functional content.

requirement_text: If the CND contains an ISIM/UICC it shall support the AKA authentication method (TS 187 001 [8])
rationale: Supporting a named authentication method is a conditional function and a security mechanism. Its FR label differs from the NFR treatment of authentication support in row 3172. The referenced standard supplies context not present in the isolated sentence.

requirement_text: The CND should support protocol for local authentication in CPN/CNG.
rationale: Support for a local authentication protocol is a security capability labelled FR. Compare NFR-labelled authentication support in row 3172. Agreement with this label does not resolve the broader convention difference.

requirement_text: The CND should be able to communicate its services related capabilities to the CNG.
rationale: Communicating service capabilities to a gateway is a specified information-exchange function. The reference and prediction have a plausible functional interpretation.

requirement_text: CNG shall be able to classify intra-LAN traffic that is simply bridged by the CNG itself within the CPN.
rationale: Classifying bridged traffic describes processing behaviour. Row 3244 contains the same wording with only a leading 'The', but is labelled NFR rather than FR. The pair makes the published standalone labels inconsistent for almost the same input.

requirement_text: The CNG shall support mechanisms for secure authentication and communication with the remote management system.
rationale: Secure authentication and communication combine security qualities with implementation mechanisms. NFR is plausible, while individual mechanisms may also be specified as functions.

requirement_text: The card issuer and the CEP card share a secret key to generate and verify MACs
rationale: Sharing a secret key and generating/verifying message authentication codes describe a cryptographic design and operations. The supplied NFR label is understandable as security, and the FR output captures operational content.

requirement_text: Unloads are permitted only to an account controlled by the card issuer and are performed only at a load device under the control of the card issuer
rationale: Restricting unloading to issuer-controlled accounts and devices could be an access-control constraint or a transaction business rule. Full system context is needed to distinguish those readings.

requirement_text: The POS device must ensure that it is dealing with an authentic card and guarantee integrity of transactions and batches to the merchant acquirer
rationale: Ensuring card authenticity and transaction integrity directly expresses security properties. NFR is a plausible label under the report's quality-attribute definition.

requirement_text: These merchant acquirers must then assign unique identifiers to PSAMs
rationale: Assigning identifiers resembles a functional data-management operation, but the actor is a merchant acquirer and the sentence begins 'These'. Context is needed to tell whether this is software behaviour or an organizational rule.

requirement_text: Contain the details of a transaction between the initialize command for that transaction and the initialize command for the next transaction
rationale: Containing transaction details suggests a storage/data function, but the isolated imperative has no explicit actor. The matching FR prediction does not make the fragment self-contained.

requirement_text: Be the entity that maintains control over the flow of a transaction ensuring that all security is enforced
rationale: Controlling transaction flow is behavioural and enforcing security is a quality/security purpose. The subject is supplied by surrounding context, so an exclusive label is difficult to establish from this fragment alone.

requirement_text: Ensure that each batch of transactions is cleared and settled once and only once
rationale: Exactly-once clearing and settlement may be treated as transaction correctness/business behaviour or a reliability property. The isolated text supports both readings and omits the actor.

requirement_text: The CEP card sends a response to the reversal command to the POS device. The reversal is considered to be successful even in the event of a negative response or no response from the CEP card
rationale: Sending a reversal response and defining when the transaction counts as successful specify protocol and business behaviour. No service-quality target is given.

requirement_text: The aggregated totals by card issuer must be transmitted to the merchant acquirer at the same time and manner as the non-aggregated detail transactions in the batch
rationale: Transmitting aggregate totals with detailed transactions specifies message content and workflow timing. It does not state a response-time or throughput threshold.

requirement_text: Each POS transaction completed at the POS device is given a S5 MAC by the PSAM which is used by the merchant acquirer to validate that the transactions were made at a POS device with a valid PSAM. The batch total count and amount must be protected by the S4 MAC which must also be validated by the merchant acquirer
rationale: Generating and validating authentication codes are operations that protect transaction integrity. The paragraph mixes behavioural mechanisms and security constraints, so a single binary label loses part of its meaning.

requirement_text: The card verification method indicator (CVMI) in the CEP card must specify support of online PIN verification and at least one method of off-line PIN verification (encrypted or unencrypted)
rationale: Requiring support for specified PIN-verification methods is a security/protocol constraint and also a supported capability. The NFR reference is plausible but not the only possible behaviour-based reading.

requirement_text: Load acquirers must determine the currencies that they must support for load transaction
rationale: Determining supported currencies can be a business decision by a load acquirer rather than software behaviour. The sentence alone does not establish whether the NFR reference or FR prediction is semantically preferable.

requirement_text: Card issuers must provide an alphabetic currency code in each message that establishes a new currency. This alphabetic currency code and the currency exponent will be used by the load device to display currency balances. This allows the cardholder to identify the currency being displayed
rationale: Providing currency-code fields in messages to display balances specifies data and interface behaviour. The FR reference and prediction are plausible.

requirement_text: All on-line messages must have the ability to include card issuer discretionary data from the CEP card
rationale: Including issuer discretionary data in online messages specifies message content/capability. The NFR prediction disagrees with a plausible functional interpretation.

requirement_text: The card issuer must have the ability to deactivate a CEP application in the response to a load or currency exchange transaction
rationale: Deactivating an application in response to a transaction is an explicit conditional function.

requirement_text: The CEP card may support multiple currencies. Each currency occupies a ƒ??slotƒ?_x009d_ within the CEP. The slots are defined by the currency supported. The currency for an individual slot is determined during load or currency exchange. Currency exchange could apply to a single slot and then only for the total balance
rationale: Supporting multiple currencies and defining how slots are assigned specifies data organisation and transaction behaviour. The text contains encoding artifacts, which are retained and may affect processing; their causal effect is not established.

requirement_text: The CEP card limits each slot to a maximum balance. The maximum balance for a slot is established when a currency is assigned to the slot and is determined externally by the card issuer or by CEP card data which indicates a maximum balance in a reference currency. There is no requirement that all slot maximums have the same relative value and there is no requirement for the card to maintain a maximum total value
rationale: A maximum stored monetary balance is a business/data-validation rule, not necessarily a performance-capacity requirement. The limit alone does not establish NFR. The published FR label is plausible.

requirement_text: Load and unload functions must be authenticated using end-to-end security between the card and the card issuer
rationale: End-to-end authentication/security between the card and issuer states a security condition on load/unload functions. NFR is plausible, although the mechanisms implementing it will have functional behaviour.

requirement_text: Expired cards must not be used for loading electronic value
rationale: Preventing expired cards from loading value is a conditional transaction/business rule. It does not state a performance, availability or other service-quality level.

requirement_text: Load devices that are available to the general public should support multiple sources of funding and support both linked and unlinked loads
rationale: Supporting funding sources and linked/unlinked loads states supported transaction types. The FR reference is plausible and the NFR output warrants investigation.
